caption:
A brain organoid kept alive for five years matured on a schedule: fetal-like, newborn-like, then early-childhood-like gene expression, with DNA methylation clocks matching time in the dish. About 425,000 cells profiled from about 110 organoids. Resemblance is molecular, not functional. Which childhood-onset disorder would you study with it first? Faravelli, Arlotta and colleagues, Nature, 19 Aug 2026.

#neuroscience #organoids #brain #science

slides.claim: A brain in a dish, *5 years*

slides.body: Grown from stem cells and kept alive for more than five years, some to about seven.
Gene expression moved through three stages, in order, on a schedule like a growing brain.

slides.claim: Its DNA marks matched the calendar
slides.body: DNA methylation clocks read chemical marks that track age. Here they lined up with time in the dish.
From about 110 organoids, combining new and earlier data.

slides.claim: It resembles brain tissue in gene expression, not in function
slides.body: No thinking, no feeling was shown. The match is molecular.
